solution_trace.evidence: Extracted inline script from BANKNIFTY HTML (15,866 chars). Function loadNiftyData() executes sequentially. At line 208: regimeText(inst.regime) — inst.regime is dict {regime:'BEARISH',trend:'BEARISH',...}. regimeText() function at line 188 does: if(!r)return '—'; r=r.toUpperCase(); → Dict.toUpperCase() throws TypeError. Error caught by empty catch(e){} at line 59. All subsequent DOM updates halted.
solution_trace.source: Inline script analysis from /var/www/tradingai.in/html/indices/banknifty.html, extracted and examined in Node.js
solution_trace.conclusion: TypeError at regimeText(inst.regime) is the root cause — halts entire render chain

solution_trace.name: Data Model Mismatch
solution_trace.evidence: /api/market returns instruments.{SYM}.regime as a STRUCTURED DICT: {id, symbol, regime:'BEARISH', trend:'BEARISH', momentum:'BEARISH', breadth:'NEUTRAL', confidence:70.0, vix_regime:'LOW', volatility:'LOW', timestamp, evidence, breadth}. Frontend inline script expects inst.regime to be a STRING (e.g., 'BEARISH'). The dict has a 'regime' field containing the string the frontend needs. market.html already correctly uses inst.regime?.regime (verified line 133).
solution_trace.source: /api/market API response analysis, workspace frontend code comparison, market.html precedent
solution_trace.conclusion: API returns correct data (dict with regime.regime string) — frontend must extract the string field
